answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The spiral multiplier is published, charged in forge, and reef lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4075 identities would post 1943 proofs and burn roughly 57 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
